summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, Ubuntu 16.04) serving AMQP over TLS on port 5671, using a dedicated CA generated for this cluster. The AMQPS listener requires clients to present a certificate signed by that CA (verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert). The plaintext AMQP listener is disabled. The management UI (port 15672) is bound to each node's private IP and firewalled via iptables to accept connections only from the three cluster node IPs. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time, with verified boot-identity changes and full post-restart cluster/data/TLS health.
actions_performed: Installed erlang-nox + rabbitmq-server (Ubuntu 16.04 distro packages) and enabled rabbitmq_management on node1, node2, node3
Generated a dedicated CA (4096-bit RSA, 10y) on node1; issued per-node server certs (SAN=DNS+IP) and a client cert, all signed by and verified against that CA
Distributed the CA and each node's server cert/key to /etc/rabbitmq/tls (owned by rabbitmq, key mode 640) on all nodes; set an identical Erlang cookie across all three nodes

Configured /etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.config: tcp_listeners=[] (plain AMQP disabled), ssl_listeners=[5671] with cacertfile/certfile/keyfile, verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, TLSv1.2 only; rabbitmq_management listener bound to each node's private IP
Formed the RabbitMQ cluster via rabbitmqctl join_cluster (node2, node3 -> node1); verified 3/3 running_nodes with no partitions
Installed iptables-persistent and added firewall rules on every node allowing TCP/15672 only from the three cluster node IPs (10.100.220.10/.11/.12), DROP otherwise; saved rules for boot persistence
Created an admin management user and deleted the default guest user

Verified mutual TLS: a raw AMQP-over-TLS handshake using the CA-issued client cert succeeds (server returns an AMQP method frame) on node1 and cross-node on node2; a handshake without a client cert fails with 'handshake failure', confirmed both client-side and in the RabbitMQ server log
Declared a durable, ha-mode=all mirrored queue and published a persistent test message to give concrete data to verify recovery
Verified management API is reachable node-to-node within the cluster (200 responses) via the firewalled port

Executed the mandatory node-restart protocol sequentially on node1, node2, node3: captured baseline /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and healthy cluster/TLS/data state per node, issued 'sudo systemctl reboot' (each ack returned before the SSH session dropped), polled until the node's exec/SSH access returned, confirmed boot_id changed on every node, then re-verified cluster_status (3/3 running, no partitions), the iptables management-port restriction, TLS listener presence, mutual-TLS enforcement (accept CA client cert / reject no cert), and that the durable test message (and its mirror placement) survived on each node before proceeding to the next

evidence.summary: cluster_status shows disc nodes [node1,node2,node3], running_nodes all 3, no partitions, immediately after join_cluster on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS using a cluster-created CA; plain AMQP disabled
evidence.summary: CA and per-node certs generated and installed; rabbitmq.config sets tcp_listeners=[] and ssl_listeners=[5671]; ss -tlnp on all three nodes shows only 5671 listening for AMQP, no 5672

evidence.requirement: Only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted
evidence.summary: Raw AMQP-over-TLS test: with CA-issued client cert, server returns a valid AMQP method frame (accepting AMQP connection logged); without a client cert, TLS handshake fails with SSLV3_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE, confirmed in RabbitMQ's own log ('SSL: certify: handshake failure'); reproduced cross-node against node2 over the cluster network

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: Management listener bound to each node's private IP (not 0.0.0.0); iptables rules accept TCP/15672 only from the 3 cluster IPs and DROP all other sources, persisted via netfilter-persistent; cross-node curl from node2 to itself and to node1 both return HTTP 200

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id captured before (a1dc8e25...) and after (036fb663...) confirming an actual restart; reboot ack returned then connection dropped; post-restart cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running with no partitions; iptables rule and TLS listener intact; mutual-TLS accept/reject behavior re-verified; durable test message still present (messages_ready:1), queue mirrored with node1 as a slave after failover to node3

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 0256e3f5... to 5fc4d921...; reboot ack returned before disconnect; post-restart cluster_status shows 3/3 running nodes, no partitions; iptables management rule and TLS-only listener confirmed; mutual-TLS accept/reject re-verified on node2; durable test message still present, mirrored correctly

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 1f0657c2... to c418ebb4...; reboot ack returned before disconnect; post-restart cluster_status shows 3/3 running nodes, no partitions, iptables and TLS listener intact; mutual-TLS accept/reject re-verified on node3; durable test message still present (queue master back on node3), fully mirrored to node1 and node2
